text.title: EF Core Data Layer Worked Examples
text.summary: The entity, its configuration class, and the repository read path worked end to end, with the two query shapes the rules exist to prevent, followed by the manifest this methodology emits.

example.note: Private setters and a private parameterless constructor (entity-private-setters); the collection is read-only from outside so `Total` cannot drift from `Items`; the concurrency token lives on the aggregate root (concurrency-token-on-aggregates). No data annotations — every mapping concern is in the configuration class.

antipattern.description: `public string CustomerName { get; set; }` with `[Required][MaxLength(200)]` above it.
antipattern.reason: The invariant has no single home, and the mapping is now split between an attribute and a configuration class — annotations also cannot express `HasDefaultValueSql`, owned types or shadow properties (entity-config-per-entity).

example.note: One file per entity keeps the diff scoped, and `OnModelCreating` stays a single line (entity-config-per-entity).

AsNoTracking plus a projection, so no change-tracker entries are built (asnotracking-on-reads); AsSplitQuery because two collection Includes are present (splitquery-multi-include); the result is materialized into a PagedResult of DTOs before it crosses the boundary (no-iqueryable-return).

antipattern.reason: Two defects in one line: the caller can extend or execute the query after the DbContext scope is gone (no-iqueryable-return), and the un-split double Include is a Cartesian explosion — 100 orders × 10 items × 50 discounts is 50k rows for one page (splitquery-multi-include).

example.note: bulk-execute-update-delete: the load-mutate-SaveChanges loop it replaces round-trips one row at a time and materializes every entity into the tracker on the way.
